verdict_note: From reading only (no build, no tests). The delete cascade itself holds. page.delete with content, Layers > Delete of a threaded frame, and the group delete each plan on clones and validate the records against the successor. Each commits as ONE layout step whose inverse quotes the whole document and the decoded records, so undo restores frames, threads, layers and records together. Folio's validate_layout requires existing, reciprocal, acyclic links and one chain per story, so a wrong relink can never commit. The defects are in the new flow features and in the edges of the cascade. F1 (high): smart reflow of a story that does not end the document draws margin frames over the following existing pages, including pages that hold other stories, instead of adding pages. Its delete_empty_pages only looks at the document's trailing pages, and the facing-page pairing counts pages instead of checking spreads. F2: delete_empty_pages removes pages through the layout editor's own PageEdit::DeletePage, which the lane's own V4-06 list names as not fixed. It leaves frame records and section starts behind, so it is a new, unlisted site of the lane's failure class. F3: longdoc records that are keyed to a removed table's cell story or a removed note's story survive the cascade. Folio does not check longdoc story ids, so they validate, and a re-minted STXT id brings them back on an unrelated story. This breaks the documented 'a delete never leaves a stale entry'. F4: the lane claims STU-LAY-020/123 and MT-30696/30697, but smart reflow runs on demand only and four of the six controls are not taken. F5 to F9 are low. Verdict on id reuse: see answers.id_reuse. It is not a defect of the thread, layer-record or undo paths. It becomes live only through F3.

findings.what: STU-LAY-020 and the STU-LAY-123 smart_text_reflow row say reflow adds or removes PAGES as a threaded story grows or shrinks. The grow branch reuses flow.auto from the thread's last frame, so it first fills every page that follows in document order with a new margin frame threaded into the story. That includes pages that hold other stories' frames. Pages are appended only after the document's last page. The shrink branch considers only the document's trailing pages, so a story in the middle of the document never loses a page. Pairing counts pages. A facing document that ends on a lone left page (every even page count: [R1],[L2]) gets R3, which completes the spread. Because one page is odd, it then also gets L4, a new lone spread with an empty threaded frame. delete_empty_pages can never remove L4, because doomed = [L4] is odd and is popped. Each call reports changed=true in one undo step, so the damage is undoable but silent.
findings.scenario: (a) layout of 3 pages. Story A is a frame on page-1, overset. Story B is a frame on page-2 with text. Run layout_flow.smart_reflow {frame: A, delete_empty_pages: false, preserve_facing_page_spreads: false}: a new frame threaded from A covers B's frame on page-2, page-3 gets one, and pages are added after page-3. (b) Run layout_flow.smart_reflow with delete_empty_pages=true after shrinking A: nothing is removed, because page-3 is the last page and holds an empty A frame, but the walk then meets page-2, which holds B. (c) A facing document [R1],[L2] with the story on L2 needing one more page: 2 pages are added (R3, L4), and L4 holds an empty frame that delete_empty_pages keeps.
findings.fix: Smart reflow inserts new pages directly after the page of the thread's last frame (PageEdit::InsertPage after that page) and draws frames only on pages it inserted. Record the reading as UNVERIFIED D5: InDesign has an 'add pages to end of story/section/document' choice that is not among the six captured controls. delete_empty_pages removes the run of pages after the last page with composed lines when those pages hold nothing but empty frames of this story, wherever that run sits in the document. preserve_facing_page_spreads decides by spread completeness: add a partner only when the inserted run leaves a lone page in its spread, and remove only whole spreads. autoflow flow.auto and flow.fixed_page_auto share the 'next existing page' rule. That is InDesign parity for autoflow (UNVERIFIED D5), so state it in the docs and leave the rule.
findings.test: layout_delete_cascade.rs, new test smart_reflow_inserts_after_the_story_and_never_covers_another_story: (a) as the scenario, assert that no layer whose story is A sits on B's page, that the new pages follow page-1 in page order, and that there is one step layout.smart_reflow. (b) Shrink A, run smart_reflow with delete_empty_pages, and assert that the inserted pages are gone, B's page is untouched, and page count = 3. (c) Facing [R1],[L2]: assert pages_added == 1 and that the last spread is [L2, R3].

findings.what: Records keyed to a story that is removed only as an owned cell or note story are kept. These are a footnote or index mark inside a table's cell story, an index mark or table inside a footnote's note story, and an endnote in a cell story. Their story is dropped from records.stories. LayoutRecords::validate (session layout_records.rs:154-196) passes them, because neither the longdoc validator nor the records validator checks longdoc story ids against self.stories, and they are saved. A nested note's own note story is also kept as an orphan. The layout editor's mint then hands the freed STXT id to the next drawn frame's story, and the stale footnote, index mark or table attaches to that unrelated story at its old byte offset.
findings.scenario: Package: frame F shows story S. Table T in S has cell story C. A footnote has story_id C and note story N. An index mark sits in N. delete_layer(F): the footnote {story_id: C, note_story_id: N} and the index mark in N remain, and N stays in records.stories while C is gone. Then layout.draw_frame mints STXT id C for the new frame's story, and the new story renders a footnote reference with N's text.
findings.fix: In cascade_layout_delete, first compute the closure of removed stories: start from the unshown stories, add the cell stories of tables and the note stories of footnotes, endnotes and sidenotes keyed to a story in the set, and repeat until nothing changes (bounded by the record counts). Then drop every story-keyed longdoc and flow record and the stories themselves by that closure. Optional, outside the owned paths: LayoutRecords::validate refuses a longdoc story id that self.stories does not hold, so the fail-closed guard covers what the cascade misses.
findings.test: containers.rs unit test or layout_delete_cascade.rs with a hand-built package as described: after delete_layer(F), no longdoc record names S, C or N, records.stories holds none of them, and layout.draw_frame plus the editor's footnote and index listing show nothing on the new story. Undo restores the entry byte for byte.

answers.id_reuse: Not a defect of this lane's thread, layer-record or undo paths, and not a blocker on its own. (1) Threads: Folio validate_layout (crates/hsk-studio-folio/src/layout.rs:582-650) requires existing, reciprocal, acyclic links and one chain per story, so no kept frame can keep a link to a freed id that a new frame later takes. (2) Layer-keyed layout records (frame_options, vertical_thresholds, applied_object_styles, anchored_objects, graphic_frames, running_texts frame ids, parent items, Replace overrides) are all checked against the document's layers (layoutflow.rs:917-939 and :1036-1040; longdoc.rs:1696 and :1872; parentpages.rs:209 and :287). Any the cascade missed would refuse the commit, so none survives to attach. (3) History is linear and each layout step quotes the whole document and records, so undo across a reuse removes the newer frame before it restores the older one. Session revision entries of deleted layers are kept by design (session.rs:2266-2269) and undo refreshes them. (4) Placed raster layers mint from their own block after pruning (place.rs:1170-1192), and Viewer deletes drop component records (records_after_delete). It IS live in one place: F3. Longdoc records keyed to nested cell or note stories survive, Folio does not check longdoc story ids, and the editor's STXT mint (layout_ui.rs:950-959) re-mints the freed story id, which resurrects them on an unrelated story. Fix F3 in this lane. The mint itself belongs to layout_ui.rs (SMB-TYPE-CHARACTER-ATTRIBUTES-1's file) and should, as a follow-up, avoid ids named by the undo/redo history's layout documents and by stored records, as harness-core's page mint does. The acd73bc7 test change is acceptable in substance, because a process test should not pin minted ids. But it was not re-run, and nothing asserts that a reused id carries nothing of the deleted frame (F3's test covers that).
